discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Feynman's idea of simulating quantum physics with controllable quantum systems became a laboratory reality through ultracold atoms in optical lattices. Zoller and coworkers showed theoretically (1998) that atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters, and set out a broad programme for analog quantum simulation. Bloch, with Greiner, observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), the first clean realization of a strongly correlated lattice model in a fully controllable system. Greiner and Bloch then developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution, giving direct images of correlations, entanglement, antiferromagnetic order and many-body dynamics in Hubbard models. Together they founded a new field: quantum many-body physics studied by engineering the Hamiltonian itself. It now addresses high-temperature superconductivity models, many-body localization, thermalization and lattice gauge theories, and is a central pillar of today's quantum technologies.
